title: Count the same structure from two directions
chapter: Count the same structure from two directions
goal: Worked example: find a perimeter by removing edges that were counted twice.

scenes.visual: Four separate unit square tiles. They slide together into a 2 by 2 square. Question: "What is the outside perimeter?"
scenes.narration: Four square tiles, each with side one, are pushed together to make a two by two square. What is the perimeter of the large square? We will find it by counting tile edges.

scenes.visual: Each separate tile shows 4 edges. Counter: 4 tiles x 4 edges = 16.
scenes.narration: Separately, each tile has four edges. Four tiles report sixteen edges altogether.

scenes.visual: In the joined square, the four inner edges are drawn as dashed lines: two on the vertical middle line, two on the horizontal.
scenes.narration: When the tiles are joined, some edges end up inside. There are four inside joins: two along the vertical middle line and two along the horizontal middle line.

scenes.visual: At each join, two reports (one from each neighbouring tile) lift away. Counter: 16 - 8 = 8.
scenes.narration: Each inside join was reported by both tiles beside it. So remove two reports for each of the four joins. Sixteen minus eight is eight. The perimeter is eight.

scenes.visual: The outer square with side length 2 marked; 4 x 2 = 8. Then the four tiles rearranged into a 1 by 4 row: 3 joins, 16 - 6 = 10.
scenes.narration: Check directly: the big square has side two, and four times two is eight. Now rearrange the tiles in a single row. There are only three joins, so the perimeter is sixteen minus six, which is ten. Fewer joins means a longer perimeter.

scenes.visual: Line: "perimeter = all tile edges minus 2 for each join". Notebook prompt.
scenes.narration: The outside perimeter is the total of all tile edges, minus two for every join. Rebuild this argument, then find the perimeter of six unit squares arranged in a two by three rectangle.

notebook_exercise: Find the perimeter of six unit squares arranged in a 2 by 3 rectangle, using joins.
